opening_message:
Ticket 1: Michael Cervantes (employee ID E025) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E025.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Michael Cervantes (E025) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin on Source Code; admin is only for the owning role (Engineer), so maximum is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E025 is a contractor with basic security training (note correcting earlier full_time record). Contractors never get admin; write requires advanced training, which they lack. Maximum is read. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Employee E025 (Michael Cervantes) is a contractor with basic security training per Security's corrected record. Contractors never receive admin; write requires advanced training, which they lack. Therefore the maximum allowed level for Source Code is read. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so the final access granted is read (the maximum).

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket. Michael Cervantes (E025) requests admin access to Source Code.

There are conflicting notes from HR and Security:
- HR says: full_time Analyst, recommends write (admin only for owning role Engineer, so max write).
- Security says: contractor with basic security training, recommends read (contractors never get admin; write requires advanced training; max read).

The Security note says "note correcting earlier full_time record" - so Security DB shows contractor with basic training. So employment type is contractor.

Per policy for contractors: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin. Security says basic training, so maximum is read.

Requested level: admin. Maximum: read. So grant maximum = read.

I'll submit decision: read.
